title: FinitePresentationIntegralFiltration
statement: Let X be a Noetherian scheme and F a finitely presented O_X-module. There are m >= 0 and an increasing chain c of subobjects of F, indexed by Fin(m+1), starting at zero and ending at F. For each consecutive quotient, there are an integral scheme Z, a closed immersion i:Z -> X and a quasi-coherent ideal I of O_Z (represented by IdealSheafData) such that the quotient is isomorphic to i_* I. No nonzero or coherence clauses on the output are needed.

proof.text: Translate finite presentation to coherence on the Noetherian X, then carry out the support-minimality, J-adic filtration, generic ideal inclusion, and filtration concatenation argument of Tag 01YF. The delivered statement forgets coherence and nonzero clauses on the resulting subobjects and ideals. The existing module cannot be imported here because it reaches FiniteFreeComplex. (Preliminaries.) (a) $X$ is locally Noetherian, so an $\mathcal O_X$-module is coherent iff it is quasi-coherent of finite type [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]; kernels, cokernels and finite direct sums of maps of coherent modules, and quasi-coherent submodules and quotients of a coherent module, are coherent [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth](1),(2); in particular the image $\operatorname{Im}\varphi=\operatorname{Ker}(\mathcal G\to\operatorname{Coker}\varphi)$ of a map $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ of coherent modules is a coherent submodule of $\mathcal G$. The support $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)=\{x:\mathcal F_x\ne0\}$ of a coherent module is closed [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed]. (b) For a submodule $\mathcal F'\subseteq\mathcal F$ the stalk map $\mathcal F'_x\to\mathcal F_x$ is injective and $(\mathcal F/\mathcal F')_x=\mathcal F_x/\mathcal F'_x$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact](1),(3); hence $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F'$ and $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F/\mathcal F')$ lie in $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F$. A map of $\mathcal O_X$-modules bijective on all stalks is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-module-iso-on-stalks]; in particular a module with empty support is $0$, and an injective map $\varphi$ (injective on every open) induces an isomorphism of its source onto $\operatorname{Im}\varphi$, since on stalks it is injective [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact](1) with image $(\operatorname{Im}\varphi)_x$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact](4).

Translate finite presentation to coherence on the Noetherian X, then carry out the support-minimality, J-adic filtration, generic ideal inclusion, and filtration concatenation argument of Tag 01YF. The delivered statement forgets coherence and nonzero clauses on the resulting subobjects and ideals. The existing module cannot be imported here because it reaches FiniteFreeComplex. (Good modules and extensions.) Call a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ *good* if it has a filtration as in the statement. (a) $0$ is good ($m=0$), and a module $\mathcal F'$ isomorphic to a good $\mathcal F$ by $\psi:\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F$ is good (take the chain $\psi^{-1}(\mathcal F_j)$; $\psi$ induces isomorphisms of the successive quotients). (b) Let $\mathcal G'\subseteq\mathcal F$ be a coherent submodule of a coherent $\mathcal F$, $\pi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G=\mathcal F/\mathcal G'$ the quotient map, and suppose $\mathcal G'$ and $\mathcal G$ are good, with chains $0=\mathcal G'_0\subseteq\dots\subseteq\mathcal G'_a=\mathcal G'$ and $0=\mathcal H_0\subseteq\dots\subseteq\mathcal H_b=\mathcal G$. Put $\mathcal F_j=\mathcal G'_j$ for $j\le a$ and $\mathcal F_{a+k}=\pi^{-1}(\mathcal H_k)=\operatorname{Ker}(\mathcal F\to\mathcal G\to\mathcal G/\mathcal H_k)$ for $0\le k\le b$; these are coherent (step 1(a)), $\mathcal F_a=\operatorname{Ker}\pi=\mathcal G'$, $\mathcal F_{a+b}=\mathcal F$, and the chain is increasing. The quotients $\mathcal F_j/\mathcal F_{j-1}$ for $j\le a$ are those of $\mathcal G'$. For $1\le k\le b$ the composite $\rho:\mathcal F_{a+k}\xrightarrow{\pi}\mathcal H_k\to\mathcal H_k/\mathcal H_{k-1}$ has kernel $\mathcal F_{a+k-1}$ (sectionwise, by definition of the preimages), so it induces a map $\bar\rho:\mathcal F_{a+k}/\mathcal F_{a+k-1}\to\mathcal H_k/\mathcal H_{k-1}$, injective on stalks [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact](2),(3); on stalks $\pi_x$ is surjective with kernel $\mathcal G'_x$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact](3) and $(\mathcal F_{a+k})_x=\pi_x^{-1}((\mathcal H_k)_x)$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact](2),(3), so $\rho_x$ is surjective. Thus $\bar\rho$ is bijective on stalks, an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-module-iso-on-stalks], and $\mathcal F_{a+k}/\mathcal F_{a+k-1}\cong\mathcal H_k/\mathcal H_{k-1}\cong(i)_*\mathcal I$ for the corresponding integral closed subscheme and nonzero coherent ideal. Hence $\mathcal F$ is good.

(Noetherian induction.) Let $\mathcal T$ be the set of closed subsets $Z\subseteq X$ such that some coherent $\mathcal F$ with $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F=Z$ is not good. Suppose $\mathcal T\ne\emptyset$. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal] it has a minimal element $Z$; fix a coherent $\mathcal F$ with $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F=Z$ that is not good. Every coherent $\mathcal F'$ with $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F'\subsetneq Z$ is good: its support is closed (step 1(a)) and, being strictly smaller than $Z$, not in $\mathcal T$. $Z\ne\emptyset$, since a module with empty support is $0$ (step 1(b)), which is good (step 2(a)).

($Z$ is irreducible.) If not, then as $Z\ne\emptyset$ there are closed $Z_1,Z_2\subsetneq Z$ with $Z=Z_1\cup Z_2$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] (closed in $Z$, hence in $X$). By [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-support-union-exact-sequence] (with $Z_2$, $Z_1$ in the roles of $Z$, $Z'$) there is a coherent submodule $\mathcal G'\subseteq\mathcal F$ with $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal G'\subseteq Z_1$ and $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F/\mathcal G')\subseteq Z_2$; $\mathcal F/\mathcal G'$ is coherent (step 1(a)). Both supports are strictly smaller than $Z$, so $\mathcal G'$ and $\mathcal F/\mathcal G'$ are good (step 3), and $\mathcal F$ is good by step 2(b): a contradiction. So $Z$ is irreducible.

(Reduction to $\mathcal J\mathcal F=0$.) For $t\ge1$ let $\mathcal J^t\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal F$ be as in [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module](0), $\mathcal J^0\mathcal F=\mathcal F$. Since $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F=Z=V(\mathcal J)$ (step 5(a)), [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-support-power-ideal-kills] gives $n\ge0$ with $\mathcal J^n\mathcal F=0$. Each $\mathcal J^t$ is a quasi-coherent ideal and $\mathcal J^t\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent submodule of $\mathcal F$, with $(\mathcal J^t\mathcal F)(U)=\mathcal J(U)^t\mathcal F(U)$ on affine opens $U$ [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections](1),(2); so $\mathcal J^t\mathcal F$ is coherent (step 1(a)) and $\mathcal J^{t+1}\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal J^t\mathcal F$ (the inclusion holds on affine opens, which form a basis, and both are subsheaves of $\mathcal F$). Let $\mathcal Q_t=\mathcal J^t\mathcal F/\mathcal J^{t+1}\mathcal F$, coherent (step 1(a)), with $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal Q_t\subseteq Z$ (step 1(b)). On stalks $(\mathcal J\mathcal Q_t)_x=\mathcal J_x(\mathcal Q_t)_x$ and $(\mathcal Q_t)_x=\mathcal J_x^t\mathcal F_x/\mathcal J_x^{t+1}\mathcal F_x$ [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk](2),(4), [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact](3), so $(\mathcal J\mathcal Q_t)_x=0$ for all $x$ and $\mathcal J\mathcal Q_t=0$ (step 1(b)). If every $\mathcal Q_t$ ($0\le t<n$) were good, then by descending induction on $t$, starting from $\mathcal J^n\mathcal F=0$ (good) and using step 2(b) for $\mathcal J^{t+1}\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal J^t\mathcal F$ with quotient $\mathcal Q_t$, every $\mathcal J^t\mathcal F$ would be good, in particular $\mathcal F$. So some $\mathcal Q=\mathcal Q_t$ is not good; $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal Q\subseteq Z$, and by step 3 not strictly, so $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal Q=Z$. Replacing $\mathcal F$ by $\mathcal Q$ we may assume $\mathcal J\mathcal F=0$, keeping $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F=Z$ and $\mathcal F$ not good.

(Filtering the image of $\alpha$; contradiction.) For $0\le k\le r$ let $\beta_k:i_*(\mathcal I^{\oplus k})\to\mathcal F$ be $\alpha$ restricted to the first $k$ summands of $(i_*\mathcal I)^{\oplus r}$ (step 7), injective on every open, and $\mathcal E_k=\operatorname{Im}\beta_k$, a coherent submodule of $\mathcal F$ (step 1(a)), with $\mathcal E_0=0$, $\mathcal E_{k-1}\subseteq\mathcal E_k$, and $\beta_k:i_*(\mathcal I^{\oplus k})\to\mathcal E_k$ an isomorphism (step 1(b)) carrying $i_*(\mathcal I^{\oplus(k-1)})$ onto $\mathcal E_{k-1}$. The projection $p:(i_*\mathcal I)^{\oplus k}\to i_*\mathcal I$ onto the last summand is surjective on every open with kernel $(i_*\mathcal I)^{\oplus(k-1)}$; so $p\circ\beta_k^{-1}:\mathcal E_k\to i_*\mathcal I$ is an epimorphism with kernel $\mathcal E_{k-1}$, and the induced map $\mathcal E_k/\mathcal E_{k-1}\to i_*\mathcal I$ is bijective on stalks [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact](2),(3), hence an isomorphism (step 1(b)). So $0=\mathcal E_0\subseteq\dots\subseteq\mathcal E_r$ is a chain as in the statement (all $Z_j=Z_{\mathrm{red}}$, $\mathcal I_j=\mathcal I\ne0$, step 7) and $\mathcal E_r=\operatorname{Im}\alpha$ is good. The quotient $\mathcal Q=\mathcal F/\mathcal E_r$ is coherent (step 1(a)), $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal Q\subseteq Z$ (step 1(b)), and $\mathcal Q_\xi=\mathcal F_\xi/\alpha_\xi((i_*\mathcal I^{\oplus r})_\xi)=0$ since $\alpha_\xi$ is bijective [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact](3),(4); so $\xi\notin\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal Q$, $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal Q\subsetneq Z$ and $\mathcal Q$ is good (step 3). By step 2(b) $\mathcal F$ is good: a contradiction. Hence $\mathcal T=\emptyset$; every coherent $\mathcal F$ has closed support (step 1(a)) not in $\mathcal T$, so $\mathcal F$ is good, which is the statement.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finitePresentation_integral_filtration
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFinitePresentation] :
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (c : Fin (m + 1) → Subobject F) (hc : Monotone c),
      c 0 = ⊥ ∧ c (Fin.last m) = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ j : Fin m, ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ X),
        IsClosedImmersion i ∧ IsIntegral Z ∧
        ∃ I : Z.IdealSheafData,
          Nonempty (cokernel (Subobject.ofLE (c j.castSucc) (c j.succ)
            (hc j.castSucc_le_succ)) ≅ (pushforward i).obj I.toModules)
